title: Demo Environment Kickoff Notes (Demo Tenant + Talk Track + Deck)
content:
Kickoff: Redwood Demo Environment ("demo tenant")

Date/time
- Tue 2025-10-21, 10:00–11:00 PT

Attendees (live)
- Talia Benson (PM, program)
- Markus Klein (SE, demo technical owner)
- Simran Kaur (enterprise demo architect)
- Soojin Lee (PMM)
- Camila Reyes (marketing sponsor)
- Alex Martinez (DevEx sponsor)
- Ethan Park (control plane/auth)
- Sean Gallagher (SRE lead)
- Dylan Brooks (Console/tooling sponsor)
- Mei Lin (demo data pipelines)
- Avery Johnson (AE pilot)

Why we’re here (problem statement)
- Demos are currently "person-dependent" and brittle:
  - Quota/429s show up mid-call
  - Auth/RBAC misconfig locks people out
  - Console dashboards are empty (no traffic / wrong project / ingestion delays)
  - Model catalog changes or rollout impacts the output live
  - Capacity constraints or region-level issues break streaming
- We need a repeatable environment + a standard run-of-show so any AE/SE can deliver the same story with minimal setup.

Goals (what success looks like)
1) A production-like demo tenant with prebuilt, known-good scenarios that cover:
   - Core API (chat, streaming, structured output, tool calling)
   - Production economics (batching/caching levers, token-level cost/latency)
   - Reliability (fallback routing + graceful degradation)
   - Observability (Console dashboards, traces, error analysis, rollouts)
   - Enterprise/security (mostly narrative + screenshots)
2) Fast reset + easy parallelization:
   - Reset time in minutes (target: <10 min, stretch: <5 min)
   - Support 2–4 parallel demos without cross-contamination
3) Stable even when the real product moves:
   - Pin model versions for demo routes
   - Controlled, explicit fallback policy
4) Safe and compliant:
   - Synthetic data only
   - Least-privilege keys, short-lived creds where possible
   - Clear rules on recording/screensharing

Non-goals (explicitly out of scope for v1)
- Building a full customer POC environment (separate motion; demo tenant should not become a quasi-prod POC)
- Guaranteeing “benchmark-perfect” latency numbers in every network condition (we’ll show distributions + explain variance)
- Live editing of advanced routing policies during the demo (we can show pre-configured policies + console screenshots for advanced cases)

Scope (v1 deliverables)
A) Demo tenant foundation
- Dedicated demo org + projects (namespacing for parallel demos)
- Seeded routes + model pins + fallback behavior
- Synthetic traffic generator to populate dashboards reliably
- Reset automation (one command) + healthcheck output

B) Demo scripts + artifacts
- Standard 30-minute demo run-of-show (AE/SE handoffs)
- Standard deck with live steps + backup screenshots
- Talk track script with branching (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private narrative)
- Demo certification checklist (pass/fail) and training plan

C) Runbooks + escalation
- Reset runbook
- Capacity/quota runbook
- "What broke" playbook (empty dashboards, streaming disconnects, 401/403, model unavailable)
- Demo environment SLOs + alert routing

Primary personas we’re optimizing for
- App engineer: “Can I integrate in an afternoon? Is output controllable? Does streaming/tool calling work?”
- ML/platform lead: “Can I keep latency predictable? Can I lower cost with batching/caching? What about fallbacks and rollouts?”
- Security reviewer: “SSO/SAML? RBAC? audit logs? retention/residency? private/VPC?”
- Procurement/finance: “How pricing works, commitments for Dedicated, what controls exist to cap spend?”

Known-good scenarios (initial list)
NOTE: these are the candidate scenarios we’ll freeze in PM-197. Outputs must be deterministic enough to be demo-safe, but not so canned that it feels fake.

1) Core API demo (live, 7–10 min)
- Chat completions with streaming
  - Show time-to-first-token + cancellation
  - Show retries behavior (client-side) for transient errors
- Structured output
  - JSON schema or equivalent; show validation + “repair” story if model deviates
- Tool calling
  - Simple tool: "get_shipping_status(order_id)" or "lookup_account_balance(customer_id)"
  - Emphasize production controls: tool timeout, max tool calls, logging/tracing
- SDK snippets
  - Python + TypeScript; pinned SDK version for demo stability

2) Production economics demo (live, 7–10 min)
- Same prompt set under two configurations
  - A) latency-optimized (lower batching, cache on)
  - B) cost-optimized (more batching, cache on; maybe quant profile preconfigured)
- Show token-level breakdown in Console
  - total tokens, output tokens, cache hit rate (if available), avg latency, p95 latency
- Explain what’s actually controllable by the customer vs what Redwood auto-optimizes

3) Reliability + graceful degradation (live, 5–7 min)
- Preconfigured route with a pinned primary model
- Demonstrate fallback routing
  - Capacity-constrained simulation (synthetic) OR a "flip" in demo config that triggers fallback safely
  - Show what stays constant (API contract) + what changes (model variant, region)
- Talk track: “we degrade gracefully without taking your app down”

4) Observability + operations (live + screenshot fallback, 5–8 min)
- Console: dashboards
  - latency and cost charts populated (last 1h/24h)
  - error rate chart with a small, intentional synthetic error spike to discuss error analysis
- Tracing hooks
  - show an example trace (request timeline, streaming timeline if supported)
- Rollouts view
  - canary or A/B test (pre-seeded) with clean “winner/rollback” narrative

5) Enterprise/security (narrative + screenshots, 3–5 min)
- SSO/SAML overview + RBAC roles
- Audit log examples (screenshots; avoid sensitive internal IDs)
- Retention controls and data residency talk track
- Private/VPC architecture diagram (static)

Open questions (parking lot)
1) Model pinning + demo stability
- Which model families are we comfortable anchoring the demo to for 60–90 days?
- What is our “safe fallback” definition (same family only? same context length? same tool-calling support?)
- How do we alert if the pinned model is deprecated or capacity changes?

2) Console/dashboard seeding
- What minimum volume is needed to make graphs look “real” without being noisy?
- How do we keep the distributions stable (time-of-day, region, request types)?
- Do we seed rollouts history (fake but consistent) or generate it with a background job?

3) Reset + parallel demos
- Do we create a project per SE, per demo, or per region?
- How do we prevent “someone else’s demo traffic” from showing up in the same dashboard view?
- Credential approach: one shared key w/ scopes vs per-SE keys rotated automatically

4) Compliance / safe sharing
- What’s explicitly OK to show live (audit logs? user list? API keys page?)
- Minimum viable “security FAQ” one-pager for enterprise calls

5) Pricing talk track boundaries
- Where reps have flexibility vs what requires approvals (POC credits, discounting)
- How to talk about Dedicated-like controls in a demo tenant without misleading SKU claims

Decisions made in the meeting (tentative)
- We will build a dedicated demo tenant (not reuse internal staging) to reduce surprise breakage and improve access control.
- We will prioritize stability over breadth: fewer scenarios, well-instrumented, with strong backup mode.
- The live demo path must always have a "no-click" fallback (screenshots/recordings) for each major section.
- Demo data must be synthetic; no importing of anonymized customer logs (still too risky).

Risks / common failure modes (from SE + AE feedback)
- 429 throttling or quota mis-sizing during parallel demos
- Streaming disconnects / region-level network flakiness
- Empty dashboards (no traffic, wrong time range, ingestion delay)
- RBAC mapping issues (SE can’t access org)
- Model output drift after a backend change (especially for structured output)

Proposed timeline (rough)
- Week 1: finalize narrative + persona mapping; freeze v1 scenarios (PM-197)
- Weeks 2–4: demo tenant build (provisioning, seed data, model pinning/fallback, traffic gen)
- Weeks 3–5: deck + talk track; record backup demo
- Weeks 5–6: training + certification; pilot with 3 AEs/SEs; fix top issues
- Ongoing: monthly refresh + on-call process for demo outages

Action items (next steps)
- Talia: create a single source of truth doc for v1 requirements + acceptance criteria (link to PRD) (due 10/24)
- Markus: draft demo run-of-show (30 min) w/ live steps + backup steps (due 10/28)
- Simran: propose enterprise/security module content + which screenshots we need (due 10/28)
- Soojin: first pass at the story arc + slide outline (problem → economics → reliability → ops → enterprise) (due 10/29)
- Alex: confirm SDK versions to pin + stable code snippets for Python/TS (due 10/29)
- Ethan: outline RBAC + key management approach for demo tenant; propose least-privilege scopes (due 10/30)
- Sean: propose demo SLO targets + escalation path + what is “demo Sev2” (due 10/30)
- Dylan/Mei: outline dashboard seeding approach and required telemetry events; define “freshness” checks (due 11/01)

Notes / rough talk track bullets captured live
- "We don’t sell a model. We sell predictable inference." (Soojin)
- Economics section should focus on levers customers care about: caching, batching, routing policy, model/quant profiles — and show the effect in Console.
- Reliability: frame fallback as a product feature, not a fire drill. Show the policy and show that API contract stays the same.
- Enterprise: keep it crisp; don’t let it hijack the entire call. Offer follow-up security deep dive.

Appendix: demo tenant naming (placeholder)
- Org: redwood-demo
- Projects: demo-core, demo-econ, demo-reliability, demo-observability, demo-enterprise (or per-SE variants: demo-<initials>-<date>)
